chart.title: Share of smartphone use by adults, 2022

text: The pie chart illustrates how adults divided their smartphone use among six main activities in 2022. The categories are shown as percentages of the total.
Overall, communication activities took up more than half of the total, while practical services such as shopping and banking accounted for a relatively small share.

Messaging was the most common use, representing 32% of the total, and social media came second at 24%. Together, these two activities made up 56% of smartphone use, which shows how important communication is for adults. Watching video and listening to music was the third most popular choice, at 18%, so messaging was nearly twice as large.

By contrast, the remaining three categories were much smaller. Web browsing accounted for 11%, and shopping and banking for only 8%. The category labelled 'other' was the smallest, at 7%, which suggests that most people use their phones for a limited number of purposes. In total, the three smallest categories made up only 26% of smartphone use, which was less than the share taken by messaging and social media together.
